_about: Judged scores for the trial (meaning drift, WOLF's tone, engineer gender neutrality, placeholder/format safety, length). Judged by Claude (claude-opus-5-5), who is also translator (a): that is a conflict of interest, so the Claude column is cross-checked against Codex's independent back-translation and Apple's, and NO score here replaces a native speaker. Automated measures are in scores.json; this file lists only what a reader judged. Scale: issues counted per 12 lines; 'major' = a player would understand something different or the line is broken; 'minor' = right meaning, wrong nuance, register or term consistency.

length_flags: needs a CJK font; width not measurable with game fonts

claude: es-419 L07 'su palabra' reads as his / your(usted) / their: both back-translators (Codex: 'their word'; Apple: 'your word') caught it. Rule needed: disambiguate a third-person possessive when it is not the addressee.
es-419 L08 'desde el control' is vague where Codex used the glossary label SOLTAR TANQUE; L09 'la caída' (the fall) for 'the drop' is a slight drift.
de L08 'vom Auslöser' shortens the station name TANKAUSLÖSER; the glossary check missed it because 'the release' is not a listed term. Glossary must list short references to stations too.
ja L07 'あいつ' (that guy) for the Director is a register choice for Nathanial, not an error. WOLF's first-person pronoun (俺 vs 私 vs 僕) is likewise his decision.
es-419 L04 'Quédate junto a SOLTAR TANQUE': a verb-shaped station label makes the death-card sentence awkward. The glossary choice, not the translator, caused it; a noun label may read better.
codex: es-419 L07 has the same 'su palabra' ambiguity as Claude.
de L05 'klemmt' (jams) for 'is stiff' changes what the player expects from the handle: caught by Claude's back-translation ('is jammed').
de L04 'im Offenen' is unidiomatic ('im Freien' / 'ungedeckt'); de L12 'Die Tür fliegt weg' reads slightly comic.
ja L02 'セーブ開始。' is clipped for a UI note; acceptable but terser than the rest of the UI.
apple: Meaning: 'draw it' (lure) became 'draw a picture' in all three languages (L09: dibujaría / zeichnen / 描かなかった); 'the door goes' became 'the door closes' (es, ja L12) and ja L12 'call' became a phone call (電話); ja L04 'out in the open' became 'naked' (露わ); ja L10 'タンクリリーゼ' is not a word; ja L11 'Your call' became 'please consult us'; de L11 'vent' became 'replace' (austauschen).
Gender: es-419 L09 '...cronometró el descenso solo' genders the engineer masculine, the exact failure the line was chosen to test.

Register: de uses formal 'Sie' in hints and the death card (L03, L04) where the style packet asks for 'du'; es L02 'La guardado' and L12 'esperar' are ungrammatical. Apple has no glossary, style or context input at all, which is why its terms drift (TANKFREISCHALTUNG, LIBERACIÓN DEL TANQUE).

As a back-translator Apple is noisy: 'WOLFt want' (its skip-translation span split a German verb), '判断は任せる' back as 'Leave the judgment to me' (inverted; the Japanese was right), and it adds pronouns Japanese never had ('where he couldn't hide'). Its round-trip of its OWN output scored the highest chrF (59.5 vs 51-52) while being the worst translation: a same-engine round trip confirms itself.
